root.name: Scotch Game: Sea-Cadet Mate
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. c3 dxc3 5. Nxc3 d6 6. Bc4 Bg4 7. O-O Ne5 8. Nxe5 Bxd1 9. Bxf7+ Ke7 10. Nd5#

overview: A trap in the Göring Gambit: after 6.Bc4 Bg4 7.O-O Ne5 8.Nxe5 Bxd1 9.Bxf7+ Ke7 10.Nd5# White mates with the knights and bishop. Black's 6...Bg4 and 7...Ne5 are errors; the real Göring Gambit plays 5...d6 or 5...Nf6 with an open game. The root records the trap, not a main line.

white_ideas.idea: Open lines with c3 and develop fast with Bc4 and Nxc3
Exploit Black's greed with Nxe5 and Bxf7+

black_ideas.idea: Take on c3 and consolidate with ...Nf6 and ...d6

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after the d-pawn exchange, White gambit pawn on c3 returned

character.notes: Quick development against a Black king that gets mated on move 10.

gambit.notes: In the Göring Gambit Black takes on c3 and may keep the pawn; this line is the trap.

soundness.notes: The Göring Gambit is sound; the trap line loses for Black.

approach.notes: The Göring Gambit is a respectable choice; the trap is a side line.

level.notes: A short trap, but the Göring needs known theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: Göring Gambit main lines
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. d4 exd4 4. c3 dxc3 5. Nxc3
sublines_that_differ.how: Black develops with ...Nf6 or ...d6 and avoids the mate; open and sharp but not a forced loss.

character.reason: Gambit lines and a quick mating trap.

gambit.reason: c3 is a pawn Black can take and keep.

soundness.reason: The Göring Gambit is playable; the trap line itself loses for Black.

structure.reason: The d-pawns are exchanged and lines are open.

approach.reason: The Göring Gambit is respectable although less common.

level.reason: A gambit with tactical lines and some theory.
